answer: Each identity must write its claim as a sonnet: fourteen lines, each stating one checkable step, written in saffron ink mixed only from its own verified jobs of this epoch. The ink fades after one tide, so a claim written in last epoch's saffron is ignored outright. The tide itself is set by the last close's hash, so no one can mix tomorrow's shade in advance. A faded line — ink that does not match this tide's shade — drops the claim and stains the sonnet unreadable; ten voices need ten fresh sonnets and ten fresh dyes.
